intentSummary: Use this page when the real question is no longer whether local AI can run at all, but whether a 24GB+ workstation path is worth validating before you commit to local hardware. The page separates high-VRAM usefulness from power, cooling, runtime, exact-card, and workload evidence.
decisionPrompts: Will the target workload repeatedly need more than a 16GB planning tier?
Is the workload frequent enough to justify local system complexity?
Can the runtime stack support the GPU vendor and exact workflow?
Have power, connector, cooling, case, RAM, and storage constraints been checked?
Would a short cloud test reduce uncertainty before local hardware commitment?

quickVerdicts.title: 24GB+ local path can make sense
quickVerdicts.description: Use this path when the workload is frequent, data-control matters, the model or image workflow needs clear headroom, and the system can support sustained GPU load.

quickVerdicts.title: Test first when fit is uncertain
quickVerdicts.description: Use cloud or borrowed-hardware validation when the workload is near a memory boundary, runtime behavior is unclear, or the exact GPU variant may create power or thermal risk.

quickVerdicts.title: Do not treat VRAM as the whole build
quickVerdicts.description: A high-VRAM card still needs connector, PSU, case, cooling, OS, driver, framework, RAM, storage, and workload checks before the plan is hardware-ready.

decisionRows.localPath: Repeated local runs, private data, and long-running experiments can justify deeper workstation validation.
decisionRows.testFirstPath: One-off experiments or occasional large jobs should be validated in cloud before local complexity grows.

decisionRows.localPath: Move into 24GB+ planning when 16GB estimates are close to the limit or the workflow needs clear headroom.
decisionRows.testFirstPath: If the estimate only barely exceeds 16GB, validate the exact model, context, image settings, and runtime before choosing a tier.

decisionRows.localPath: A CUDA-first path may be easier to validate when the workload and framework are already known.
decisionRows.testFirstPath: AMD, Intel, newer GPUs, or unusual frameworks need extra runtime checks before local hardware commitment.

decisionRows.localPath: Local planning is stronger when PSU, connector, case clearance, airflow, RAM, and storage are already mapped.
decisionRows.testFirstPath: If the system would need major rebuild work, use a validation run before narrowing exact cards.

workloadRows.usefulWhen: The model, quantization, and context path need more headroom than a 16GB page can comfortably plan around.
workloadRows.riskSignal: Long context, MoE behavior, offload, or package format can change memory needs; verify with the calculator and model-specific pages.

workloadRows.usefulWhen: Resolution, model size, extension stack, or repeated local runs make 16GB feel constrained.
workloadRows.riskSignal: Extensions, batch growth, cache, and runtime settings can break a simple VRAM estimate.

workloadRows.usefulWhen: You expect repeated experiments, local files, privacy needs, and enough system support for sustained GPU sessions.
workloadRows.riskSignal: A workstation plan is weak if storage, RAM, cooling, and driver/runtime setup are still unknown.

workloadRows.usefulWhen: A cloud run has already shown the workload fits a high-VRAM tier and is frequent enough to revisit local planning.
workloadRows.riskSignal: Do not translate cloud success into local readiness until exact GPU variant and system constraints are checked.

systemConstraints.title: Power delivery and connectors
systemConstraints.description: Check PSU headroom, PCIe connector requirements, adapter handling, and exact board-partner guidance before assuming the system can support the GPU.

systemConstraints.title: Cooling and sustained load
systemConstraints.description: A high-VRAM workstation may run long sessions. Validate airflow, case spacing, fan noise tolerance, and thermal behavior under sustained work.

systemConstraints.title: Case and motherboard fit
systemConstraints.description: Confirm GPU length, slot thickness, connector clearance, PCIe slot placement, and whether other cards or storage devices block airflow.

systemConstraints.title: RAM, storage, and local workflow
systemConstraints.description: Plan for model files, image outputs, cache, datasets, logs, offload paths, and normal multitasking outside GPU VRAM.

validationWorkflow: Estimate the target model or image workflow before comparing high-VRAM GPUs.
Classify the result as comfortable 16GB, borderline 16GB, 24GB+ local path, or cloud-test-first.
Run the exact model, context, image settings, extensions, or runtime stack when the result is close to a tier boundary.
Review GPU profile source fields and exact-card constraints instead of relying on a model name alone.
Check PSU, connector, cooling, case clearance, RAM, storage, OS, driver, and framework support before hardware commitment.

faq.question: Is 24GB VRAM enough for a local AI workstation?
faq.answer: It can be enough for some local AI paths, but the answer depends on the exact model, quantization, context length, image settings, runtime, and overhead. Use 24GB as a planning tier, then validate the workload.

faq.question: Should I compare RTX 3090 and RTX 4090 for local AI?
faq.answer: Yes, if you are evaluating 24GB CUDA-first paths. Compare source-backed GPU fields, exact-card constraints, power and cooling requirements, and workload validation needs rather than treating the pair as a simple ranking.

faq.question: Can AMD 24GB cards work for high-VRAM AI planning?
faq.answer: They can be part of the planning set when VRAM capacity is important, but runtime, framework, OS, and workload support need extra validation before the card is treated as a practical local fit.

faq.question: When should I test cloud GPU before building locally?
faq.answer: Test cloud first when the workload is occasional, the estimate is near a memory boundary, runtime behavior is uncertain, or the local build would require major system changes before you have evidence.
